tickets.subject: nf-300 ipsec tunnel blackholing during rekey on p2 site link
tickets.description: CivicWorks Public Agency called TAC after a site-to-site VPN on a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.8 started dropping traffic for short intervals while the tunnel still appeared established. The caller said the outage usually lasts 10 to 20 seconds and happens after the tunnel has been up for several hours, which initially looked like a peer stability issue. During triage, `show crypto ikev2 sa` showed the IKE SA in ESTABLISHED while the child SA counter reset during rekey, and the device log included `%IKEV2-3-PROPOSAL_MISMATCH`. The peer-side team reported repeated ESP rekey failures, and the symptom pattern matched a child-SA renegotiation problem rather than a full IKE teardown.
tickets.resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-3101 and applied the documented workaround on both peers: keep the PFS group unchanged, disable child SA rekey, and schedule a controlled tunnel restart after the change. On the Nimbus NF-300, TAC entered `config`, set `crypto ikev2 child-sa rekey disable`, and committed the change. The tunnel stabilized after the manual restart and no further traffic blackholes were observed.

tickets.subject: intermittent vpn outage on nf-300 after pfs change
tickets.description: Evergreen Clinic Network opened the case from an on-site field engineer working on a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.8. The report was that a healthcare site VPN stayed up most of the day, then briefly stopped passing traffic even though the dashboard still showed the tunnel as connected. Initial review showed the IKE SA remained up while the child SA renegotiated, and the device log contained `%IKEV2-3-PROPOSAL_MISMATCH`. The timing lined up with rekey activity, so TAC suspected a stale proposal set being reused after a recent PFS change on the peer.
tickets.resolution: TAC mapped the behavior to KB-3101 and implemented the workaround rather than changing the platform release. The customer was instructed to keep the same PFS group on both peers and disable child SA rekey on the Nimbus NF-300 with `crypto ikev2 child-sa rekey disable` under `config`, followed by `commit`. After a coordinated tunnel restart, the VPN remained stable and traffic resumed normally.

tickets.subject: site-to-site vpn drops during esp rekey on 5.0.9 firewall
tickets.description: Cornerstone Supermarkets escalated through the NOC after users on one branch link reported brief application hangs every few hours. The affected device is a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.9, and the branch tunnel was described as 'up but not moving packets' during the event. TAC found that `show crypto ikev2 sa` kept the IKE SA in ESTABLISHED while the child SA was being recreated, and the event log showed `%IKEV2-3-PROPOSAL_MISMATCH`. Because the outage was short and self-clearing, the initial suspicion from the NOC was a WAN flap, but the pattern matched a rekey negotiation failure instead.
tickets.resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-3101 and applied the supported workaround. The customer was told to leave the PFS group unchanged, disable child SA rekey on the Nimbus NF-300 using `config`, `crypto ikev2 child-sa rekey disable`, and `commit`, then perform a manual tunnel restart during a maintenance window. After the restart, the branch tunnel stopped blackholing traffic during rekey and the NOC closed the incident.

tickets.subject: branch vpn instability resolved by software upgrade to 5.1.3
tickets.description: BlueRiver Credit Union reported repeated short VPN interruptions on a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.9, with the issue affecting a branch-to-datacenter tunnel used for transaction processing. The customer noted that the tunnel stayed established for long periods and then briefly failed to pass traffic, but there was no full disconnect alarm from the peer. TAC review showed the child SA counter resetting during rekey while the IKE SA remained established, which pointed to a rekey negotiation defect rather than a routing issue. The case notes referenced a known child-SA proposal handling problem in this release family, and TAC recommended moving to a fixed release instead of continuing with a temporary workaround.
tickets.resolution: TAC identified KB-3101 and advised the customer to upgrade the Nimbus NF-300 from 5.0.9 to 5.1.3, where the child SA proposal list is rebuilt on every rekey exchange. After the upgrade and a controlled tunnel clear, the VPN completed multiple rekey cycles without traffic loss. No workaround was left in place after validation.

tickets.subject: rekey failures on nf-300 fixed after moving to 5.1.3
tickets.description: IronGate Freight called TAC by phone about a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.9 that was protecting an operational tunnel to a warehouse site. The caller initially described the problem as 'random packet loss,' but packet captures and device counters showed the loss only during IPsec rekey windows. TAC confirmed that `show crypto ikev2 sa` held the IKE SA in ESTABLISHED while the child SA restarted, and the logs included `%IKEV2-3-PROPOSAL_MISMATCH`. The symptoms matched a proposal mismatch during CREATE_CHILD_SA, especially after a recent PFS group change on the remote peer.
tickets.resolution: TAC linked the case to KB-3101 and recommended upgrading the Nimbus NF-300 to 5.1.3, the first fixed release for this issue. The customer completed the upgrade and then cleared the tunnel so both peers renegotiated cleanly with the rebuilt proposal list. After validation, rekey traffic completed without drops and the case was closed.
